svg.aria-label: Dependency diagram: The roadmap, stage by stage. 31 nodes, 44 edges. Most connected: S22 Stage 22 steam (6), S10 Stage 10 userspace drivers (5), S19 Stage 19 hyprland fidelity (5).
svg.title: The roadmap, stage by stage

g.title: Workspace, the quality gates ported from Starling, CI, the first host-testable libraries.

The third architecture, joined after stage 3 and brought through stage 4: the same loader converted ELF to PE32, a 32-bit layout argued rather than shrunk, LPAE as a paging geometry, device tree only, traps without mode stacks.
UEFI loader in Rust to a kernel Rust entry point, zero bootstrap assembly.
Buddy allocator, heap, vmap arena with guard pages and stacks, identity map dropped, W^X sweep, boot memory reclaimed, empty slab pages returned.
Vectors on every architecture, one dispatch above them; LAPIC, I/O APIC, HPET (TSC/PIT fallback); GICv2 and the architected virtual timer; the facade's irq::register, timer::after and trap::Frame.

Every processor online: INIT-SIPI-SIPI and a real-mode trampoline, PSCI CPU_ON through an identity map of the entry; a record per processor; every "one CPU" global now a lock; IPIs; TLB shootdown where hardware does not broadcast; grace periods.
Task, kernel stacks, context switch, per-CPU runqueues, the class stack, EEVDF in src/lib/kernel/sched-fair.
AddressSpace, VMOs, the VMA tree as a process map, demand paging, copy-on-write, the ELF loader, the ring-3/EL0/USR transition.
Syscall entry on every architecture, the dispatch table, the core surface: memory, files, process, threads and futex, signals with sigaltstack and rt_sigreturn, time, identity.
Inode and dentry caches, the mount table, fd sharing rules, tmpfs, devfs, procfs, cpio initramfs.
Handle tables, Channel with handle passing, Port, Interrupt, IoMapping, Job; the 0x1000 syscalls.
Placed after Networking without a number of its own: nothing on rustc's path needs it, since std targets static musl.
Enumeration, IOMMU domains, devmgr, the shared-ring block protocol, virtio-blk as a user process.
Block core, then btrfs stage A.

Placed after stage 12 without a number of its own, built on 2026-09-24 in the shape the customer chose that day: an in-kernel view like procfs and cgroupfs, fed by the services that own each fact, with bind and unbind sent to devmgr to decide (docs/SYSFS.md).

A display core and a virtio-gpu driver in ring 3 behind /dev/dri/card0, an input core and a virtio-input driver behind /dev/input/eventN, and the calls a Rust event loop makes: epoll, eventfd, FIONBIO, memfd sealing, AF_UNIX with SCM_RIGHTS.
Placed after stage 11 without a number of its own, as the ARMv7-A port sits after stage 4.
btrfs stage B.
The compositor itself: the Wayland wire protocol and its server, xdg-shell, wl_shm, the dwindle and master layouts, a CPU renderer, hyprland.conf and the hyprctl socket.

Seven namespaces (mount, user, UTS, IPC, cgroup, pid, network), the unified cgroup hierarchy with cpu, memory, io and pids as built, cgroupfs, classic-BPF seccomp with the interpreter in src/lib/, and Syscall User Dispatch.

What makes a Hyprland rather than a tiling compositor: animations with bezier curves, rounded corners, blur, shadows, opacity rules, special workspaces, groups, multiple monitors, plugins -- and the GPU behind them.

g.title: Placed after sysfs without a number of its own, asked for by the customer on 2026-09-23 (docs/CHROME.md).
SoftRt and HardRt: FIFO/RR, threaded interrupts, PI mutexes, EDF with CBS admission, the runtime mode switch with its quiescence protocol.
Steam on Ferrix, put on the roadmap by the customer on 2026-09-18 as the step after the GPU decision; a guest's stage first, on Path A's GPU, that does not wait for bare metal.
Ferrix on bare metal with an NVIDIA card driven by Ferrix itself: Path B of the GPU decision of 2026-09-18, opened when the customer wants real hardware.
The customer's design "Yoru WM" as the desktop's look and shell on hyprix (docs/DESKTOP.md section 6, 2026-10-24; docs/roadmap/stage-25-yoru.md).
Static musl busybox as /bin, a working init, job control, ttys, pipes.

g.title: The Windows game Arknights: Endfield on Ferrix, through Wine with DXVK on NVIDIA's Vulkan, put on the roadmap by the customer on 2026-10-10 as the road after Steam.

The game path: a fullscreen game faster on Ferrix than on a stock Linux desktop on the same hardware, in the time from an input to the picture that shows it and in how even the frames are under a background load.
The remaining syscall surface, the memory scale, the spawn path for rust-lld, a sysroot on btrfs.
Build Ferrix on Ferrix; the image the hosted compiler produces boots and passes every test above.
